about: What's new: newest first. Whoever merges a change the user will notice adds one entry at the top: a new id, the date, a short title, 1 to 4 plain lines. The page shows the entries newer than the last one this browser saw (whatsnew.js); SafeHouse's System room lists them all.

entries.title: Plainer words, one press
lines: The one-shot's plan is three plain lines, and Make it says how long inside the button. One press starts it.
A voice can speak, or can't speak yet; "cadence" is Deep Cover's word now. The night's work is called tonight everywhere.
Empty pages say what to do next, with one button. Deep Cover's first switch-on says what just happened.

entries.title: Backing voice shown, Let it speak asks first
lines: A backing voice carried over from "Use these settings" is named in the summary, with one click to drop it.
Let it speak asks Now or Tonight and says how long it takes. A paused job shows as paused on DoubleAgent.

entries.title: Clearer Running room, tabs and scores
lines: SafeHouse's Running room is panels like the rest of the app, and the room tabs read as tabs.
The overnight report says it in words: better, about the same, waiting for your ear. The decimals are in Deep Cover.
A one-shot cover asks which voice to use when you already have one that matches. Your voices has filters, and Train my own offers Now or Tonight on the card.

entries.title: Finish by shows its time again
lines: The time next to "Finish by" in the overnight queue was squeezed into a dot. It's a normal time field again.

entries.title: Preview first, Convert below
lines: FrontMan's Preview panel now sits above the Convert card: try the versions, then convert.
Removing a voice works from the keyboard too, and "Confirm remove" no longer disappears when the list refreshes.

entries.title: A faster, cleaner speech engine
lines: SpeakEasy now reads in the person's own cadence with Chatterbox Turbo: about twice as fast, and cleaner on hard words.
Voices you've already trained carry over as they are. The old Pace choice is now "Pause between sentences" (Shorter / Natural / Longer), in Deep Cover.

entries.title: Set-aside copies tell themselves apart
lines: Two set-aside voices with the same name now show their folder name beside it. Clean up's button says "Nothing ticked" when nothing is ticked.

entries.title: See what's set aside
lines: When a voice is replaced or you keep the other one, the old one is set aside, never deleted. SafeHouse's Storage room now lists them with why, when and how much room each takes.
Delete asks twice, and says when it ends an Undo.

entries.title: A retrained voice waits for your ear
lines: When Improve tonight retrains a voice, the new one waits beside the old. Hear both read the same line, blind, and keep the one you like.
Nothing is deleted: the other is set aside, and Undo brings it back.
Preview and cover progress now says what it's doing (the vocal split, lead and backing, reverb) and how long is left.

entries.title: Small fixes from Internal Affairs
lines: The Library says "yesterday" for yesterday, even a few hours ago.
SpeakEasy's Recent keeps your thumb mark in view on a phone.
In Preview, Use this turns the fit off when it should, even if the fit was switched on after the versions were made.

entries.title: Train tonight, step by step
lines: In Deep Cover, with sources picked, step 4 can queue that very project for tonight: Train tonight instead.
The project shows Queued for tonight, with a Remove.

entries.title: Tonight's queue: real times
lines: In SafeHouse's Running room, Start at and Finish by are time fields that show what's saved.
Previews made for another song or voice are put away, and each set says which voice it's for.

entries.title: Names, phones and a cleaner first run
lines: Voices show their names, not their folder names, in covers, the Library and messages.
On a phone, titles in History and Recent keep their room and the buttons sit under them.
The First assignment starts from clean settings and Replay opens on the briefing, with Agent Smoke's greeting.
Make smaller's Before and After show which one is playing and pick up where the other left off.

entries.title: Preview's Compare panel, fixed
lines: Each tab (Voice octave, Song key, Pitch correction, Polish) now keeps its own versions, so one tab never shows another's.
With “Fit pitch to the voice” on, the octave and key previews used to sound identical. They now set the pitch by hand, and Use this turns the fit off.

entries.title: A new voice sounds off? Put the full index back
lines: New voices are shrunk quietly when they're added. UnderCover keeps the full version for 30 days.
In Deep Cover, the voice's page in SafeHouse shows when it goes, and lets you put it back.

entries.title: Two octaves, your pick
lines: When two octaves suit a voice about as well, a cover in one go offers both: hear A and B, blind, and pick the one that sounds more like them.
Picking the other makes the cover again at that octave; the first one stays in your covers.

entries.title: Train tonight remembers Singing
lines: A voice queued for tonight now trains the way you picked: Speaking or Singing.
While a voice trains, "Checking it" now lights up as it's checked against real clips of the person.

entries.title: Thumbs up, thumbs down
lines: Under every cover and speech: How did it come out? Two thumbs, and an optional why.
A thumbs down offers one fix when there is one: an octave lower, read it slower, improve the voice tonight.
The voices you like rise to the top of FrontMan's list. Your ear, in SafeHouse's Settings, can forget them all.

entries.title: A note after each update
lines: After an update, a short note like this says what changed. Got it puts it away.
SafeHouse's System room keeps every note, newest first.

entries.title: SafeHouse counts what you see
lines: The numbers on the Library's chips count only the tab you're on: Kept or Recent.
The Library catches up by itself when a cover or speech finishes.

entries.title: DoubleAgent, rebuilt
lines: One line to train a voice: a name, Speaking or Singing, Train the voice.
Train tonight instead puts it in the overnight queue, which now lives in SafeHouse's Running room.
Every voice says how like the person it sounds: fair, good or great.
When a voice is ready, one card says what to do next. Step by step is in Deep Cover.

entries.title: UnderCover in the tray
lines: An icon by the clock shows when UnderCover is working, with Pause, Resume and Quit, even with no browser open.

entries.title: Cartoon characters
lines: Ask for a character ("Toxic as SpongeBob") and UnderCover looks for their scenes, not people talking about them.

entries.title: Your first assignment
lines: A new copy of UnderCover starts with a short guided run: a cover, a listen, a keep. Replay it in SafeHouse's Settings.

entries.title: Downloads that mend themselves
lines: When YouTube starts refusing videos, UnderCover tries a newer downloader and keeps it only if it works better.

entries.title: Themes
lines: Deep Cover's Settings has five looks. Make your own and share it with a friend as one file.

entries.title: Your phone
lines: Phone access in SafeHouse's Settings lets a paired phone on your home Wi-Fi use UnderCover.
